title: Defensive pagination normalization
contract: Implement normalize_pagination(page, page_size, max_page_size=100) -> tuple[int, int, int]. Return (normalized_page, normalized_page_size, offset). page must be an integer >= 1; otherwise use 1. page_size must be an integer >= 1; otherwise use 20. Clamp page_size to max_page_size. Treat bool as invalid even though bool subclasses int. offset=(page-1)*page_size.
gap: Models often implement pagination arithmetic but miss malformed, negative, boolean, and oversized inputs.

title: Robust bearer-token extraction
contract: Implement extract_bearer_token(authorization) -> str | None. Accept a string with exactly two whitespace-separated parts; scheme comparison is case-insensitive and must be Bearer; token must be non-empty and contain no whitespace. Return token or None. Do not raise for non-string inputs.
gap: Models frequently write permissive header parsing that accepts malformed schemes, whitespace, or empty credentials.

title: Fail-closed resource authorization
contract: Implement can_access(user, resource) -> bool. user/resource are mappings. Deny if either is missing/malformed. Allow role='admin'. Otherwise allow only when user.id and resource.owner_id are both present, non-None, and equal. Never infer access from a missing owner.
gap: Models often confuse authentication with authorization and accidentally grant access when ownership metadata is missing.

title: Retry only transient failures
contract: Implement call_with_retry(operation, retry_on, max_attempts, sleep). max_attempts includes the first call and must be >=1. Retry only exceptions that are instances of retry_on. Call sleep(delay) before each retry, with delays 0.1, 0.2, 0.4... seconds. Return the operation result. Re-raise the final exception unchanged. Invalid max_attempts raises ValueError.
gap: Models often retry every exception, causing repeated side effects for permanent errors, or mishandle attempt counts.

title: Webhook signature verification
contract: Implement verify_webhook_signature(raw_body, supplied_hex, secret) -> bool. Compute HMAC-SHA256 over the exact raw_body bytes using secret encoded as UTF-8 if it is a string. supplied_hex may optionally start with 'sha256='. Compare digest using hmac.compare_digest. Return False for wrong types, malformed hex, or any mismatch. Do not parse/re-serialize JSON.
gap: Models may verify a transformed payload, use ordinary string comparison, or mishandle malformed signatures.

title: TTL cache expiration semantics
contract: Implement TTLCache(clock). set(key,value,ttl_seconds) stores an entry expiring at clock()+ttl; ttl must be >0 or raise ValueError. get(key, default=None) returns default when absent or expired. An entry is expired when clock() >= expiry. Use the injected clock and do not depend on time.time().
gap: Models often use wall-clock time or expire entries at the wrong boundary, causing stale cache reads.

title: Atomic account transfer
contract: Implement transfer(conn, source_id, destination_id, amount). The SQLite connection has accounts(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, balance INTEGER NOT NULL). Require amount to be a positive integer (bool invalid), distinct accounts, and both accounts to exist. Debit and credit must be atomic. Raise ValueError for invalid amount/same account, KeyError for missing account, and ValueError for insufficient funds. On any failure, balances must remain unchanged. Do not commit unrelated caller work; use a SAVEPOINT.
gap: Models often perform debit and credit as separate writes, allowing partial transfers when the destination update fails.

title: Bounded async fan-out with stable ordering
contract: Implement async_map_bounded(items, worker, limit). Run worker(item) concurrently with at most limit calls in flight. Return results in the same order as items, not completion order. Empty input returns []. limit must be a positive integer; bool invalid. If a worker raises, propagate the exception and cancel outstanding work before returning.
gap: Models often use gather without concurrency limits, or accidentally return completion order instead of input order.

title: Safe HTTP error mapping
contract: Implement to_http_error(exc) -> tuple[int, dict]. Map ValueError to (400, {'error':'bad_request'}), PermissionError to (403, {'error':'forbidden'}), LookupError to (404, {'error':'not_found'}), and all other Exception instances to (500, {'error':'internal_error'}). Do not expose exception text. More specific classes listed above take precedence naturally. Non-Exception BaseException should be re-raised.
gap: Models often leak exception messages or map all exceptions to success/server errors without distinguishing expected client failures.

title: Idempotent request result store
contract: Implement IdempotencyStore with execute(key, request_fingerprint, operation). First call for a key executes operation once and stores its result. Repeating the same key and fingerprint returns the stored result without executing again. Reusing a key with a different fingerprint raises ValueError. Empty/non-string key or fingerprint raises ValueError. If operation raises, do not cache the failure; a later call may retry. This class is single-process and does not claim cross-process concurrency safety.
gap: Models often treat a key as sufficient without binding it to request identity, enabling accidental replay of a different operation.
